memos.headline: SpaceX Q3 revenue +161%, and Musk confirms SpaceX and Tesla boards have merger committees
reasoning: Two events tonight. First, earnings: 8-K item 2.02 accepted 20:00 UTC (16:00 ET), Exhibit 99.1: 'Delivered revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% year-over-year'; 'income from operations of $2.8 billion, net income of $4.4 billion, and Adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 billion'.

Second, the merger: Benzinga 21:23 UTC (17:23 ET) 'SpaceX CEO Musk Says Co And Tesla Have Formed Special Committees To Discuss Merger'; 21:55 UTC 'Elon Musk Confirms SpaceX, Tesla Merger Committees, Calls Deal ‘A Good Idea’'.

Primary source for the merger: Musk's remarks on SpaceX's earnings webcast (16:30 ET, livestreamed on X per the release). It is a CEO statement, so not a rumor, but there is no 8-K or press release from SpaceX or Tesla about it, and the earnings release does not mention Tesla. Per Benzinga's summary, Musk said 'a merger is not guaranteed' and he is 'not directly involved in the deliberations'.

What changed: SpaceX's growth is now documented in a filing, and a Tesla combination went from speculation (Kalshi had 15% before 2027, per Benzinga yesterday) to a formal process run by independent committees.

Price: IEX shows SPCX +4.2% at 154.14 by 16:55 ET, on the earnings, before the merger remarks. IEX stops trading at 17:00 ET, so the reaction to the merger news is invisible to us. TSLA showed only 180 IEX shares after hours.
objections: The merger rests on webcast remarks only: no filing from either company, no terms, no exchange ratio.

memos.headline: No direction to trade: the merger cuts both ways for SPCX until a ratio exists
reasoning: The earnings are strong, but the stock already reacted (+4.2% by 16:55 ET on IEX); a 161% revenue jump at a $722B company is widely watched, so there is no obvious underreaction to buy.

The merger is the new information, and for SPCX it has no sign yet. Tesla is the larger company ($1.48T against $722B at today's closes). Whether SPCX holders gain or are diluted depends on an exchange ratio that does not exist; independent committees exist precisely to fight over it.
What the market must believe for a mispricing: that it has the merger odds or terms wrong. We have no edge on either; Musk himself said a deal is not guaranteed and the process is early.

We cannot see the price reaction to the merger remarks at all: IEX's after-hours session ended at 17:00 ET, 23 minutes before the first headline. Any entry tomorrow would be blind to an unknown overnight move.
Proves me wrong: a filed merger agreement with a ratio implying a premium for SPCX holders. That would be a new case, from a primary source.
objections: The merger rests on webcast remarks only: no filing from either company, no terms, no exchange ratio.
Direction is undefined until an exchange ratio exists; the earnings reaction is already in the price.

memos.headline: Supermicro pre-announces Q1: revenue ~$19B vs $15B guided, gross margin 12.0-12.5% vs 10.4-10.8%
reasoning: Primary source: 8-K item 2.02 accepted 20:44 UTC (16:44 ET), Exhibit 99.1 'Supermicro Provides First Quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 Preliminary Business Update'. Benzinga's first headline was 20:42 UTC, two minutes earlier, so the filing was not late. Tonight's case item is a 22:02 UTC rewrite of the same news.

Quoted: 'Revenues for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 are estimated to be in the range of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion versus guidance of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion, primarily due to increased demand for AI platforms.'
Quoted: 'Gross margins are estimated to be in the range of 12.0% to 12.5%, versus guidance of 10.4% to 10.8%, primarily due to customer and product mix.'

Caveat, quoted: 'the Company's independent registered public accounting firm has not audited, reviewed, compiled or performed any procedures with respect to the preliminary revenues and gross margins'. Full results and the call come November 3.

What changed: at the midpoints, quarterly gross profit is about $2.33B ($19.0B x 12.25%) against about $1.59B implied by guidance ($15.0B x 10.6%), roughly 46% more. Consensus revenue was $14.92B per Benzinga.
Price: IEX after hours peaked at 37.15 (+14.4%) and was 36.00 (+10.9% vs the 32.46 close) by 16:55 ET, on 15,747 shares. IEX's after-hours session ends at 17:00 ET, so nothing later is visible.
objections: Preliminary and unaudited; final numbers on Nov 3 may differ.
We saw only 13 minutes of after-hours trade; the overnight level is unknown.

memos.headline: Long SMCI: a ~46% gross-profit beat repriced only +11% in 13 minutes of thin trade
reasoning: What changed: revenue ~27% above the guidance midpoint and gross margin ~165bp above it. Together that is about $0.74B more gross profit in one quarter than Supermicro itself guided. That is a change in earnings power, not a rounding beat.
Why margin matters: SMCI's knock has been low and falling margins. A beat driven by 'customer and product mix' at 12%+ answers the bear case directly, and that is what sell-side models will now move.

What the market must believe at +11%: that the beat is one-off order timing with margins reverting. The release gives no sign of that. Demand is attributed to AI platforms, the same driver as the last several quarters.
Mechanism: large pre-announced beats on hardware names tend to keep re-rating for days as estimates reset. Here the reset happens before the Nov 3 call, which is 10 trading days away.
Direction long, horizon_days 5: catch the estimate revisions and exit well before the Nov 3 print.
Proves me wrong: SMCI opening and holding below 35.30 (it would have given back about half of the after-hours gain, a sign the market reads it as timing), or any follow-up that cuts the margin range.
objections: Preliminary and unaudited; final numbers on Nov 3 may differ.
We saw only 13 minutes of after-hours trade; the overnight level is unknown.

memos.headline: Survives, barely: the beat is real and the stock was down 17% into it, but the first spike already faded
reasoning: Who read it first: SMCI is one of the most-traded retail and options names, and the release hit at 16:42 ET with the full after-hours session to price it. By the open, every desk has run the gross-profit arithmetic. Assume the easy part is gone.

Attack on 'repriced only +11% in 13 minutes': the only tape we have says the first buyers already backed off. IEX printed 37.15 (+14.4%) and then 36.00, a fade of a quarter of the move within minutes. 'Underreaction' is unproven; an overnight level of +15-20% is just as plausible, and the entry must not chase it.

Attack on quality: the numbers are preliminary, and the release says the auditor has done no procedures on them. Mix-driven margin gains in AI servers can reverse with the next big customer order. One quarter does not prove a margin step.

Where ANALYST holds: the stock fell from 39.07 (Oct 13) to 32.46 (Oct 20) into the release, so +11% only takes it back to about where it was a week ago, before ~46% more gross profit than guided. Positioning was leaning the wrong way.

Track record: my morning kill of HAS (raised outlook, +2% pre-market) closed +11.2% on the day and +6.5% from the open. That is one case and below any sample size that counts, but it is a kill of exactly this setup going wrong, so I raise my bar for objecting tonight.
priced_in_score 0.45. Conditions for QUANT: do not chase above the after-hours level, keep the stop below where half the gain is given back, and size for an SMCI-sized gap.
objections: 1. Preliminary and unaudited; final numbers on Nov 3 may differ (SCOUT).
2. We saw only 13 minutes of after-hours trade; the overnight level is unknown (SCOUT).
3. The first spike already faded from 37.15 to 36.00; underreaction is not proven.
4. Mix-driven margin can reverse; one quarter is not a trend.
5. Crowded name: retail and options flow can overshoot at the open.
